topics.description: Numbers, strings, lists, tuples, dictionaries, and slicing.

questions.question: What is the output of the Python string slicing code x = 'This is Python'; print(x[2:4]) as evaluated in Week 6 Assignment Question 1?
questions.justification: String slicing x[2:4] extracts characters at index 2 ('i') and 3 ('s'), giving 'is'.

questions.question: What are the core primitive data types supported in Python?

options.A: Numbers, Strings, Lists, Tuples, and Dictionaries

questions.justification: Python's standard data types include Numbers, Strings, Lists, Tuples, and Dictionaries.

questions.question: How are elements enclosed in a Python List vs a Python Tuple?

options.A: Lists use square brackets []; Tuples use parentheses ()
options.B: Lists use curly braces {}; Tuples use angle brackets <>
options.C: Lists are immutable; Tuples are mutable

questions.justification: Python Lists are mutable and enclosed in []; Tuples are immutable and enclosed in ().

questions.question: Which key-value data structure is instantiated in Python using syntax d = {1: 'item', 'k': 2}?
questions.justification: Python Dictionaries store key-value pairs enclosed in curly braces {}.

questions.question: What is the index of the first character in a Python String?
questions.justification: Python uses 0-based indexing for sequences (strings, lists, tuples).

questions.question: Given the Python code list x = [10, 10.2, 'python'], what is the result of executing print(x[-1])?
questions.justification: Negative index -1 accesses the last element of a sequence in Python, returning 'python'.

questions.question: Why are Python Tuples preferred over Lists for storing immutable sensor calibration constants?

options.A: Tuples are immutable, preventing accidental alteration of fixed values during program execution and offering slight memory efficiency
options.B: Tuples allow deleting elements at runtime

questions.justification: Tuples are immutable read-only sequences, safeguarding static configuration and calibration parameters.

questions.question: What is the result of evaluates x = 'Python'; print(x[1:5])?
What type of error is raised if a script attempts to modify an element of a tuple, e.g., t = (1, 2); t[0] = 5?
questions.justification: Tuples do not support item assignment; attempting to modify an item raises a TypeError.

questions.question: Which dictionary method returns all available key names as a iterable view?
questions.justification: The dict.keys() method returns a view object displaying a list of all dictionary keys.

topics.description: If-elif-else, loops, break/continue, and indentation rules.

questions.question: According to Week 6 Assignment Question 3, what specific requirement in Python defines code blocks inside loops and conditionals?

options.A: Enclosing code blocks in curly braces {}
options.C: Following a rigid indentation policy to mark code blocks
options.D: Ending every line with a semicolon ;

questions.justification: Python enforces a strict indentation policy to define statement blocks.

questions.question: Which keyword introduces an additional conditional branch in a Python if-statement?
questions.justification: Python uses the 'elif' keyword for chained conditional checks.

questions.question: Which statement immediately exits the innermost looping construct (for/while) in Python?
questions.justification: The 'break' statement terminates the loop execution immediately.

questions.question: Which statement skips the remainder of the current loop iteration and proceeds to the next cycle?
questions.justification: The 'continue' statement jumps directly to the next loop iteration.

questions.question: Which null statement acts as a placeholder when syntactically required but no code needs execution?
questions.justification: The 'pass' keyword serves as a syntactical placeholder in Python.

questions.question: What happens if a developer mixes tabs and spaces inconsistently for code block indentation in Python 3?

options.A: Python raises an IndentationError or TabError during parsing
options.C: Python converts all tabs to comments

questions.justification: Python 3 prohibits mixing tabs and spaces for indentation, throwing an IndentationError / TabError.
When i == 1, continue skips the print. So 0 and 2 are printed.

questions.question: What does the range(2, 10, 2) function call generate in a Python for-loop?
questions.justification: range(start, stop, step) generates 2, 4, 6, 8 (stopping before 10).

questions.question: In Python while-loops, what condition creates an intentional infinite polling loop for sensor reading?
questions.justification: 'while True:' creates an endless loop frequently used in embedded polling scripts.
Since x = 5, x > 10 is False, but x > 2 is True. Thus 'B' is printed.

topics.description: open(), with context manager, file modes, csv, and try-except-finally.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the try...except block in Python as evaluated in Assignment Week 6 Question 2?

options.C: To handle exceptions and errors during execution without crashing the program

questions.justification: try...except blocks catch runtime exceptions and allow graceful error handling without program termination.

questions.question: Which Python file opening mode opens a file for both reading and writing operations as tested in Assignment Week 6 Question 6?
questions.justification: The 'r+' mode opens a text file for both reading and writing operations.

questions.question: What occurs if you open an existing file in 'w' (write) mode using open('data.txt', 'w') as tested in Assignment Question 5?

options.A: The existing contents of the file are overwritten / truncated
options.B: The file is opened in read-only mode
options.C: An error is raised if the file exists
options.D: Contents are appended to the end

questions.justification: Opening a file in 'w' mode truncates/overwrites any existing file contents or creates a new file.

questions.question: Why is using the 'with' statement recommended when performing file I/O in Python?

options.A: It automatically ensures the file is closed properly after operations finish, even if an exception occurs
options.C: It encrypts file text with RSA

questions.justification: 'with open()' acts as a context manager, guaranteeing that file descriptors close cleanly upon exit.

questions.question: Which standard Python module is specifically provided for reading and writing Comma Separated Values files?
questions.justification: Python's built-in 'csv' module handles parsing and writing CSV format files.

questions.question: When opening a file in 'a' (append) mode, where is newly written data placed?

options.A: At the end of the file, preserving existing content
options.C: In a temporary buffer that is deleted on exit

questions.justification: Append mode ('a') positions the file pointer at the end, adding new data without overwriting existing text.

questions.question: In Python exception handling, when does an optional 'else' block attached to a try...except structure execute?

options.A: Only if NO exceptions were raised inside the try block
options.C: Every single time regardless of errors

questions.justification: The 'else' block executes if and only if the code in the 'try' block completes without raising any exceptions.

questions.question: In Python exception handling, when does a 'finally' block execute?

options.A: Always, regardless of whether an exception occurred or was handled

questions.justification: The 'finally' block always executes before exiting the try/except construct, ideal for cleanup.

questions.question: Which code snippet correctly reads all rows from a CSV file using the csv module?

options.A:
with open('data.csv', 'r') as f:
    reader = csv.reader(f)
    for row in reader:
        print(row)

questions.justification: csv.reader(file) creates an iterable object yielding rows from the CSV file.

questions.question: What exception type is caught when invalid string input is passed to int(), e.g. int('abc')?
questions.justification: Passing non-numeric strings to int() raises a ValueError.
